summary: Public rulings issued by the Commissioner bind the Commissioner and protect taxpayers who rely on them from penalties and interest.
Assessable income covers ordinary and statutory income, while exempt and non-assessable non-exempt income are excluded from taxable income.
Outgoings are deductible when incurred in earning assessable income or running a business, but not if they are capital, private or domestic.
GST applies to taxable supplies made in an enterprise, but input-taxed supplies such as residential rent carry no GST and no input tax credits.
Single Touch Payroll requires employers to report wages, withholding and super to the tax office each payday.
Late superannuation guarantee charges are not deductible and unpaid amounts can make directors personally liable.
A trustee holds property for beneficiaries and, in a discretionary trust, decides who receives income or capital each year.
Division 7A treats private company payments, loans and forgiven debts to shareholders as unfranked dividends unless loans are put on complying terms.
The National Employment Standards set eleven minimum entitlements for national system employees, covering hours, leave, notice and redundancy.
Modern awards set minimum pay and conditions for an industry or occupation on top of the National Employment Standards and are reviewed by the Fair Work Commission.
Enterprise bargaining lets workplaces negotiate tailored agreements, with bargaining representatives bound by good faith requirements.
Employees who have served the minimum period and are under the income threshold or covered by an award are protected from harsh, unjust or unreasonable dismissal.
A redundancy is genuine only when the job is no longer needed, consultation obligations are met and redeployment was not reasonable.
General protections stop anyone taking adverse action against a person for having or exercising a workplace right.
Businesses must ensure worker health and safety so far as reasonably practicable, and officers must exercise due diligence.
A company is a separate legal entity that can own property and contract, and shareholders are liable only for unpaid amounts on their shares.
Directors and officers must act with the care and diligence of a reasonable person in their position.
Directors must act in good faith in the company's best interests and for a proper purpose, and accessories to breaches can also be liable.
Public companies, large proprietary companies, disclosing entities and registered schemes must prepare audited financial reports that meet accounting standards.
Companies must keep financial records that explain their transactions and allow audited statements to be prepared, and retain them for seven years.
Liquidation winds up a company and distributes asset proceeds to creditors by statutory priority, with employee entitlements paid before unsecured creditors.
Financial services businesses need an Australian financial services licence and must meet obligations on resources, competence, risk management and dispute resolution.
Market integrity rules add requirements for market participants, and insider trading means trading on inside information.
APRA supervises banks, insurers and most super funds through prudential standards on capital, liquidity, governance and risk.
AUSTRAC requires reporting entities to run anti-money laundering programs, verify customers and report suspicious and threshold transactions.
Employers must pay at least 12 percent super quarterly, and missed deadlines trigger the superannuation guarantee charge.
Unfair dismissal claims go to the Fair Work Commission within 21 days and may lead to reinstatement or capped compensation.
Every director needs a permanent 15-digit director ID, applied for personally through the Australian Business Registry Services before appointment.
GST is a 10 percent tax that businesses must register for once turnover reaches $75,000, with credits available for business purchases.
Directors must not let a company incur debts while insolvent, although safe harbour can protect those pursuing a better outcome.
Employees accrue four weeks of paid annual leave a year, while casuals receive a loading instead.
Individuals and trusts holding assets for twelve months get a 50 percent CGT discount, super funds get one-third and companies get none.
Listed entities must immediately disclose price-sensitive information unless a narrow confidentiality exception applies.
Employers pay FBT at 47 percent on non-cash benefits given to employees, in a year running from April to March.
The Corporations Act protects whistleblowers who report misconduct and requires larger companies to have a whistleblower policy.
Eligible employees can request flexible work in writing, and employers must respond within 21 days and refuse only on reasonable business grounds.
Public companies must hold an AGM within five months of year end, and listed companies vote on the remuneration report.
Payroll tax is a state tax on wages above a threshold, with grouping rules and registration in each state where wages are paid.
Directors of an insolvent company can appoint an administrator, and creditors later decide the company's future while a moratorium applies.
